outline.h2: What is a customer journey map template, and what does ours include?
outline.answerHint: A customer journey map template is a reusable grid that a team fills with user research to show how one persona moves through one scenario: journey stages across the top, and lanes for actions, touchpoints, thoughts, emotions, pain points, evidence, opportunities and owners down the side. Ours has 6 header fields, 5 editable stages and 8 lanes, and downloads free as PDF, SVG, PNG and CSV.
points: Intro before this H2 (see variety.introStyle): one template cell (Stage 2, Thinking) written two ways: a guessed sticky note vs a research-backed cell with a quote and its source ('heard in 7 of 12 interviews', illustrative). First sentence carries the keyword. Second paragraph: what the post gives (the download, a worked example, 7 steps to fill it from research). UP link in the first 300 words: anchor 'UX research services' -> /services/ux-research-services/ attached to a sentence naming UX research as the parent discipline.

Download block at the END of the intro, before H2 1 (the h2-then-text rule only governs what follows an H2): one sentence carrier 'Download the customer journey map template below in PDF, SVG, PNG or CSV' + a ul of 4 direct links (see downloadAsset.files), each link text naming the format (e.g. 'PDF, US Letter landscape'), plus one line linking the worked-example PDF.

Definition in our words, citing NN/g Journey Mapping 101 (Sarah Gibbons) for 'a visualization of the process a person goes through to accomplish a goal' (paraphrase, link). Name the parent concepts: journey mapping is a UX research method; the hub delivers 1 journey map per persona.

H3 'What is customer journey mapping?' (PAA): direct answer first sentence: the process of researching and drawing the stages a persona goes through, the actions, thoughts and emotions at each stage, and the opportunities they reveal.

Template anatomy table (intro sentence before it), one row per child concept: persona and scenario header (actor, scenario and goal, expectations, research base: methods, n, dates), journey stages (5 editable columns), and 8 lanes: Doing (actions), Touchpoints and channels, Thinking (verbatim quotes), Feeling (emotion curve on an emotion scale from -2 to +2), Pain points, Evidence lane (source + evidence level), Opportunities, Owner and metric. Visual 1 is the blank template with this anatomy annotated; its astext panel is this table.
Attributes printed here: lane count, file formats, emotion scale.

One sentence on other templates (AIO entities): Miro and FigJam boards need an account; Confluence's page template uses 4 fields per stage; HubSpot's 7 templates sit behind a form; Canva offers visual layouts. Factual, no disparagement, no links needed (cap externals).

outline.h2: How does a customer journey map differ from a user journey map and other UX maps?
outline.answerHint: A customer journey map follows one persona across the whole relationship with a company, from first awareness to renewal or support, while a user journey map follows one persona through one product task, such as first-time setup. Both come from user research; service blueprints, experience maps, empathy maps and user flows answer different questions.
points: Comparison table (intro sentence first), visual 3: rows = customer journey map, user journey map (UX journey map), experience map, service blueprint, empathy map, user flow; columns = point of view, scope, time order (chronological or not), question it answers, when to use. Source: NN/g 'UX Mapping Methods Compared' (Sarah Gibbons, 5 Nov 2017) for experience map / journey map / service blueprint / empathy map distinctions, paraphrased and cited once. Service blueprint row names frontstage, backstage and support processes.
H3 'What is a user journey?' (PAA): the sequence of steps a person takes in a product to reach one goal; the user journey map adds what they think and feel at each step.

H3 'User journey map vs user flow' (PAA, heading may use 'vs' as a label; carrier: 'the user journey map vs user flow question'): a user flow is a screen-by-screen diagram of the paths a generic user can take, with no emotions or quotes and no persona; a user journey map is one research-based persona's experience, including what happens outside the product.
Carriers for 'user journey map' and 'ux journey map' here (see keywordCarrier.secondary). State that the downloadable template works for both: rename the stages.
Do not reuse Figma's or Coursera's wording; Coursera's 'user journey map is an umbrella term' framing is not ours.

outline.h2: Which stages and lanes should your customer journey map template use?
outline.answerHint: Use the stages your user research finds for the scenario, usually 5–7, and the 8 lanes in our customer journey map template; marketing lifecycle stages (awareness, consideration, purchase, retention, advocacy) fit a brand-wide map, while a product task needs stages named after what the persona actually does.
points: H3 'What are the 7 steps of the customer journey?' (PAA): first sentence: there is no single standard; sources list 3 to 7 stages. Give one common 7-stage lifecycle set (awareness, consideration, decision, purchase, onboarding, retention, advocacy) as an option, then say why research-named stages beat it for product work. Stage count attribute.
H3 'Map types: current state, future state and day in the life': one definition each (AIO entities). The download is a current-state map by default; a future-state map reuses the grid after research.

Lanes explained one by one as a short list with what evidence each needs (no image: the anatomy is visual 1). Mention 'moment of truth' once: the stage where the emotion curve drops lowest is where the persona decides to stay or leave.
Map scope attribute: one persona and one scenario per map (NN/g one point of view; hub 1 journey map per persona). Persona count attribute (hub 2–4).
Carrier: 'A customer journey map template only saves time if every cell can point to a source.'

outline.h2: Where does the evidence for each journey map lane come from?
outline.answerHint: Each lane of a journey map needs a different kind of user research: interviews fill the thinking, expectations and quotes; contextual inquiry fills the actions, workarounds and touchpoints you only see by watching; analytics and support tickets fill drop-off and pain-point frequency. A hypothesis map built from team knowledge is a starting point, marked 'assumed'.
points: Visual 4: evidence source map (method -> lanes). Text panel = table method | lanes it fills | what it cannot tell you.

Interview count attribute: 10–15 one-hour user interviews per user group (hub). Observation count attribute: contextual inquiry with 4–6 users in the real work setting (hub), e.g. a clinic front desk. Contextual inquiry gets one sentence of definition only + the link to /blog/contextual-inquiry/ when live (that post owns the method; do not explain how to run a contextual inquiry here).

Evidence level attribute: the 4-level key heard / observed / measured / assumed, with one example each. NN/g (Kate Kaplan, 'When and How to Create Customer Journey Maps', 2016) calls journey mapping a qualitative-research process and says quantitative data alone cannot build the story: cite once, paraphrase.
Hypothesis map: NN/g cheat sheet term; a team draft from what it already knows is useful to plan the research, never a deliverable. Every hypothesis cell is marked 'assumed' in the evidence lane.

Lead moment 1 (one sentence, no client claims): the observed lane is the one teams cannot fill from a desk; our researchers run the 4–6 contextual inquiry sessions inside the hub's generative fieldwork step (7–15 days).

outline.h2: How do you fill a customer journey map template from research, in 7 steps?
outline.answerHint: Fill a customer journey map template in 7 steps: fix one persona and one scenario, collect the evidence you already have, run user interviews, observe users with contextual inquiry, tag and cluster the findings, write each lane with its evidence level, then validate the map with users and stakeholders and give each opportunity an owner.
points: ol of 7 steps, each with its output (this is the PAA answer for '7 steps to map the customer journey' and 'how do I create a user journey map'): 1 frame scope (persona, scenario, research questions); 2 gather existing evidence (analytics, support tickets, past studies) and draft a hypothesis map; 3 run 10–15 user interviews per user group (hub); 4 run contextual inquiry with 4–6 users (hub); 5 tag and cluster in Dovetail with affinity mapping (one-sentence definition; affinity mapping is a future cluster topic, no link); 6 write each lane, quote verbatims, plot the emotion curve, mark evidence levels; 7 validate (walk 2–3 participants or frontline staff through it), assign owners and metrics, set a review cadence.
Visual 5: 7-step strip with the output of each step. Text panel = the ol (do not repeat the steps a third time in prose).

Research timeline attribute: in our UX research programme these steps run inside the hub's 4–8 weeks (research framing -> recruitment -> generative fieldwork -> evaluative studies -> synthesis and readout); deep link 'our 5-step UX research process' -> /services/ux-research-services/#how-does-the-ux-research-process-work. Quote the hub step that produces the map: 'Synthesis and readout (4–7 days): Findings are tagged in Dovetail, turned into personas, journey maps and a JTBD opportunity map, and presented in a 90-minute readout.' Never assign map output to another hub step.
One body carrier with the literal keyword in step 6.

outline.h2: Customer journey map template, filled in for an illustrative clinic scheduling app
outline.answerHint: This customer journey map example follows a clinic practice manager through the first month of a staff-scheduling app, from sign-up to the first published rota; it is a user journey map of one product task, and every cell names its evidence. The clinic, the app and every number are illustrative.
points: Label as illustrative in the first sentence and in the caption (honesty: no client). Persona 'Dana, practice manager at a 3-site physiotherapy clinic' (invented). Research base line: 12 interviews with practice managers + 5 contextual inquiry visits to front desks (illustrative, within hub ranges).

Stages (research-named, 5): Sign up and import staff; Set shift rules; Build the first rota; Publish and handle swaps; Month-end hours export. Each stage: one action, one touchpoint, one quote, emotion -2..+2, one pain point (e.g. the spreadsheet workaround kept 'just in case', echoing the hub's interview example), evidence level, one opportunity with owner and metric.
Visual 2 = the full worked example (also a download, see downloadAsset). Text panel = the filled grid as a markdown table (5 stage columns x 8 lanes).
Answer the PAA 'Can you provide an example of a user journey map?' in the first two sentences (say this is one).
This section is also the 'customer journey map example' carrier. Do not borrow Deckary's industries (SaaS onboarding, skincare, orthopedic surgery, mortgage, fine dining) or HBS's T-Mobile.

outline.h2: How do you turn a journey map into decisions instead of wall art?
outline.answerHint: A journey map turns into decisions when each opportunity on it has one owner, one metric and a date, and when the team ranks opportunities by the persona's lowest emotion points and the strength of the research evidence behind them.
points: Ranking rule (our practice, not a statistic): severity on the emotion curve x evidence level (observed/measured outrank heard, heard outranks assumed). Small 3-column example from the worked example (opportunity, owner, metric).
Review cadence attribute: update after each new study or major release; keep the evidence lane dated. Living document (AIO term).

DOWN link: /case-studies/vocable/ anchor 'how we mapped the Vocable creator journey'. Use only the case study's words: the creator journey was mapped from stakeholder interviews into 4 phases (planning, drafting, optimizing, publishing) and each screen was designed around a problem heard in those interviews. Do not call them user interviews; do not cite the 35% result.
Hub trigger (hub 'when to invest' list): teams that disagree about priorities with no shared personas or journey maps. Lead moment 2 in one sentence.
Do not use the NN/g survey percentages that User Interviews quotes secondhand (27%, 13%, 13%) unless the fact-checker finds them on nngroup.com; default: leave out.

outline.h2: Which customer journey map mistakes make the template useless?
outline.answerHint: The customer journey map mistakes that make a template useless are presenting an assumption-only map as user research, mapping several personas on one grid, forcing marketing funnel stages onto a product task, drawing an emotion curve without quotes, and leaving opportunities without an owner.
points: 6 bullets (mistake + why it breaks the map + the lane or step that fixes it). Include 'too many lanes: a 14-lane map nobody reads' and 'never updated'.

Visual 6: pre-share map quality checklist (8 checks: one persona, one scenario, stages named from research, every quote sourced, evidence level on every cell, emotion curve backed by quotes, every opportunity has owner + metric, review date set). Text panel = the checklist ul. Do not repeat the 6 mistakes as the checklist; the checklist is positive pass/fail checks.

outline.h2: When should a research team build the customer journey map with you?
outline.answerHint: Bring in a research team when the journey map has to settle a product decision, the persona is hard to reach or observe, or the team's own map is mostly 'assumed' cells; our UX research programme delivers 2–4 personas with 1 journey map each, built from 10–15 interviews per user group and contextual inquiry.
points: Hub facts only (siteFacts): deliverable wording, interview and contextual inquiry counts, Dovetail synthesis, 90-minute readout, 4–8 weeks. Price once: $25,000–$60,000, linked 'what a 4–8 week research programme costs' -> /services/ux-research-services/#how-much-does-ux-research-cost. No standalone journey-map price (siteFacts.conflicts).
Deep link 'personas and journey maps our research programme delivers' -> /services/ux-research-services/#what-do-ux-research-services-include.
Sideways link: 'how to choose a UX research agency' -> /blog/choose-ux-research-agency/ for readers comparing providers (one sentence).

Closing paragraph (main leadAngle): carrier 'If you would rather not fill the customer journey map template alone, send us the hypothesis map you already have…' + /contact/ link + second UP link to the hub ('UX research services' again is fine as the end-of-post hub link, or 'our UX research programme').

faqs.q: How do you make a customer journey map in PowerPoint?
faqs.hint: PAA. First sentence direct: insert our SVG file (Insert > Pictures), right-click and choose Convert to Shape to edit each box and label, or paste the CSV into a PowerPoint table. Microsoft support confirms Convert to Shape for SVG in Microsoft 365 (cite). Mention it applies to PowerPoint for Microsoft 365 and 2019+ per the support page; fact-checker to confirm wording.

faqs.q: How do I create a user journey map?
faqs.hint: PAA, same answer as H2 5 in 2–3 sentences: pick one persona and one product task, fill the same template's lanes from 10–15 interviews and contextual inquiry, name stages after the task's steps, then validate. Link #how-do-you-fill-a-customer-journey-map-template-from-research-in-7-steps (in-page anchor; confirm the generated id after build).

faqs.q: Can you build a customer journey map template in Excel or Google Sheets?
faqs.hint: Yes. Open our CSV file in Excel, Google Sheets or Numbers: rows are lanes, columns are stages. A spreadsheet suits evidence notes and links; a visual board suits workshops. NN/g also publishes a spreadsheet journey-map template (optional mention, no link if the external cap is reached).

faqs.q: How many personas should one journey map cover?
faqs.hint: One. Each map follows one persona through one scenario; the hub delivers 2–4 personas with 1 journey map per persona. If two personas share a journey, map both and compare.

faqs.q: Can AI create a customer journey map?
faqs.hint: Yes, as a first draft only: an AI tool such as ChatGPT can propose stages and a hypothesis map, but every cell it writes is 'assumed' until interviews or observation back it. Answer starts with Yes (boolean rule). No tool comparisons.

faqs.q: How often should you update a customer journey map?
faqs.hint: After each new study or major release that touches the journey (review cadence attribute), and keep the evidence lane dated so stale cells are visible. Our practice; no invented interval statistic.
